question: What product is formed in the chlor-alkali process?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Sodium Hydroxide**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The chlor-alkali process involves the electrolysis of brine (sodium chloride solution).
 
• This process produces three primary products: sodium hydroxide (NaOH), chlorine gas (Cl₂), and hydrogen gas (H₂).
 
• Sodium hydroxide is a strong alkali used in various industries, including paper, soap, and detergent manufacturing.
 
• The process occurs in an electrolytic cell, where an electric current is passed through the brine.
 
• Sodium hydroxide is collected at the cathode, while chlorine gas is collected at the anode.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Electrolysis:**

 
 
• A process by which electrical energy is used to drive a non-spontaneous chemical reaction.
 
• In the chlor-alkali process, it involves the decomposition of sodium chloride solution.
 
 
 
• **Brine:**
 
 
• A concentrated solution of sodium chloride (NaCl) in water.
 
• Used as the raw material in the chlor-alkali process.
 
 
 
• **Chlorine Gas:**
 
 
• A by-product of the chlor-alkali process collected at the anode.
 
• Used in water purification, disinfectants, and the production of PVC.
 
 
 
• **Hydrogen Gas:**
 
 
• Another by-product of the chlor-alkali process collected at the cathode.
 
• Used in fuel cells, ammonia production, and hydrogenation of fats and oils.
